This Private Hospital, a contemporary 488-bed facility, is seeking a motivated Registered Nurse to join its Acute Medical and Coronary Care Unit (CCU). The practice environment is defined by its cutting-edge infrastructure, featuring 13 operating theatres, specialized catheter laboratories, and a state-of-the-art emergency department. Within Ward 4B—a dynamic 36-bed unit with six dedicated CCU beds and 30 high-acuity medical beds—the successful candidate will operate in a paperless environment utilizing advanced Electronic Medical Records (EMR) and MEDCHART systems. The facility is meticulously designed to optimize patient safety and operational efficiency, providing a high-functioning workspace for clinicians focused on cardiac and respiratory care. 

 The team composition is deeply multidisciplinary, consisting of leading clinical specialists and a supportive cohort of dedicated nurses. To ensure nurses can focus on delivering evidence-based care, the hospital provides extensive administrative and nursing support, alongside integrated Chronic Disease Management (CDM) services. This role offers significant clinical autonomy, allowing nurses to exercise sound clinical decision-making within a fast-paced setting. For those looking to broaden their expertise, the hospital offers exceptional special interest opportunities, including previous rotations to the Cardiac Cath Lab and Intensive Care Unit for ward-based upskilling. Additionally, staff have access to supervisor opportunities and unique pathways to pursue tertiary qualifications through specialized programs. 

 Professional growth is prioritized through comprehensive Continuing Professional Development (CPD) support, including dedicated Coronary Care and Cardiothoracic intensive study days. The hospital understands the importance of a sustainable career, offering flexible working arrangements such as 12-hour shifts to support a healthy work-life balance. Financial and wellness benefits are robust, featuring competitive hourly rates, salary packaging, and a unique bulk-billing service for employees and their immediate family members. Staff also enjoy discounted onsite parking and access to wellness programs like Fitness Passport. 

 Situated just 13km north of the Sydney CBD, the location offers unparalleled lifestyle benefits, combining the convenience of metropolitan access with the natural beauty of the Northern Beaches. The region is renowned for its vibrant outdoor culture, stunning coastlines, and community-focused atmosphere, making it an ideal setting for professionals seeking a rewarding career and an active personal life. As the facility prepares for an exciting transition into the public health network in late April 2026, successful applicants will join a "One Team" culture during a transformative period that offers unique long-term career stability and progression. We are a well-established landscaping and strata gardening company delivering high-quality outdoor maintenance and landscaping solutions across residential, strata, and commercial properties in Sydney. This role is responsible for the construction, maintenance, and ongoing care of landscaped areas across strata and commercial sites. You will work across multiple locations, delivering high- quality landscaping outcomes while ensuring safety, efficiency, and client satisfaction. This is a hands-on role suited to someone with solid horticultural knowledge, practical landscaping experience, and the ability to work independently while meeting quality and safety standards.

Key Responsibilities
Interpret landscape plans and site requirements for strata and commercial properties
Prepare landscaped areas including soil preparation, planting, turfing, and mulching
Select appropriate plants and materials based on site conditions and design intent
Install, test, maintain, and troubleshoot irrigation systems
Perform professional pruning, hedging, fertilisation, and plant health management
Maintain landscaped areas to a high standard across multiple sites

Ensure all work complies with WHS regulations, environmental guidelines, and company procedures
Liaise with strata managers and internal teams regarding scheduled landscaping works
Ensure sites are maintained to company and client standards
Report any site issues or maintenance needs
Support team members and attend scheduled team meetings

Skills & Experience
Minimum 1 years experience as a Landscape Gardener, Gardener or in commercial landscaping
Strong knowledge of plants, turf management, irrigation systems, and soil preparation
Ability to read and implement landscape plans
Experience working across strata or multi-site environments
Good time management and organisational skills
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Good communication skills for client and stakeholder interaction
Current Australian driver’s licence
Hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)
Certificate III or higher in Landscape Construction, Horticulture, or a related field (desirable)

What We Offer
Full-time, ongoing employment
Stable workload across established client sites
Supportive team environment
Opportunity to grow with a well-regarded strata landscaping business

If you are an experienced Landscape Gardener who takes pride in delivering high-quality outdoor environments and enjoys working within a professional and supportive team, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please follow the prompts and submit your resume. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Join Clean Green Strata and be part of a team committed to maintaining and enhancing outdoor spaces across Sydney.

Employer questions
Your application will include the following questions:
How many years' experience do you have in a Landscaping Role?
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a Landscape Gardener?

result.description:
Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $100,000 – $130,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting the implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of workplace health and safety systems across mining, engineering, maintenance, fabrication, and industrial projects. You will work closely with project managers, supervisors, employees, and contractors to ensure compliance with legislation, company policies, and client safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Implement, maintain, and monitor workplace health and safety systems, policies, and procedures.
•	Provide advice and guidance to management, supervisors, and employees on occupational health and safety matters.
•	Conduct workplace inspections, audits, risk assessments, and safety observations.
•	Identify workplace hazards and recommend appropriate control measures to minimise risks.
•	Assist with incident investigations, reporting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
•	Develop, review, and maintain safety documentation, including SWMS, JSA, risk assessments, and safety reports.
•	Monitor compliance with WHS legislation, Australian Standards, client requirements, and company procedures.
•	Deliver safety inductions, toolbox talks, and training sessions to employees and contractors.
•	Promote a strong safety culture and encourage continuous improvement in workplace practices.
•	Assist project teams with safety planning, mobilisation requirements, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain safety records, registers, inspection reports, and incident databases.
•	Liaise with clients, contractors, and regulatory bodies regarding health and safety matters where required.
•	Ensure compliance with workplace health, safety, environmental, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as a Safety Advisor, Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, or similar WHS role.
•	Relevant qualification in Occupational Health and Safety, Workplace Health and Safety, or a related discipline.
•	Strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation, safety management systems, and risk management principles.
•	Experience working within mining, construction, engineering, maintenance, or industrial environments is highly regarded.
•	Ability to conduct workplace inspections, audits, investigations, and safety training.
•	Strong communication, consultation, and problem-solving skills.
•	Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively with project teams.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and safety management systems.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $100,000 – $130,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing professional development and career progression.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

The location is in a  DPA-approved area , making it ideal for a wide range of candidates.
